newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Angolan oil firm could take stake in Petrogal.
newsitem.headline: Angolan oil firm could take stake in Petrogal.

text.p: Angolan state oil company Sonangol could take a stake of between five and 10 percent of the capital of Portuguese state oil company Petrogal-Petroleos de Portugal, Under-Secretary for Energy Jose Penedos said.
"We always wanted to reserve a slice of capital for Sonangol," Penedos told reporters during a trip to Oporto.
"It could take around five percent, and up to 10 percent at most," he added.

Earlier, the Economy Ministry confirmed that Portugal had reached an agreement in principle with Saudi Aramco for the Saudi Arabian state oil company to take a 27.5 percent stake in state-controlled energy group Petrogal.
Petrocontrol, the Portuguese consortium that is the state's current partner in the group, will see its holding drop from 45 percent to 27.5 percent under the accord.
The Portuguese state's holding would fall to 45 from 55 percent and the deal should be formally concluded by the end of the year, the statement added.
The state could retain a stake of around 10 percent and the remainder would be floated on the bourse, Penedos said.
Oil industry sources said that Sonangol could purchase the stake with oil and not money.
